messages.task:
You are a financial data analyst asked to reason over a structured database that contains synthetic—but internally consistent—information about employee benefit plans maintained by a multinational company.

Scenario
The company offers several types of retirement-related benefit plans (defined contribution, defined benefit, and post-retirement health & welfare) to employees across multiple regions, most notably the U.S., U.K., the Netherlands & Canada joint plan, and several continental-European countries.  Expenses are recorded each calendar year and expressed in millions of U.S. dollars.

Tools
You do NOT have direct SQL access.  Instead, you can invoke the following helper functions; combine them as needed to derive new insights.

1. list_regions() -> List[str]
   Return every geographical region for which any data exist.
2. get_region_id(name: str) -> int
   Translate a human-readable region name into its internal identifier.
3. list_years() -> List[int]
   List all calendar years present in the database.
4. get_calendar_year_id(year: int) -> int
   Obtain the internal identifier for a specific calendar year.
5. list_plan_type_codes() -> List[str]
   Return the short codes of all plan types (e.g. "DC" for defined contribution).
6. get_plan_type_id(code: str) -> int
   Translate a plan-type code into its internal identifier.
7. get_expense(region_id: int, year_id: int, plan_type_id: int) -> float
   Fetch the expense (in millions of USD) for the given region/year/plan-type trio.
8. compute_average(values: List[float]) -> float
   Compute the arithmetic mean of a list of numeric values.

Additional (potentially useful but not always necessary) helpers
• get_total_expense_region_year(region_name: str, year: int) -> float
• convert_currency(amount: float, from_currency: str = "USD", to_currency: str = "EUR") -> float

Question
Considering the years 2016–2018, what is the average expense for the significant plans in the U.K.?

When you have collected all the information you need, output ONLY the final numeric answer (truncate, not round, to two decimal places) so that it can be automatically verified.

New task:
You are a financial data analyst asked to reason over a structured database that contains synthetic—but internally consistent—information about employee benefit plans maintained by a multinational company.

Scenario
The company offers several types of retirement-related benefit plans (defined contribution, defined benefit, and post-retirement health & welfare) to employees across multiple regions, most notably the U.S., U.K., the Netherlands & Canada joint plan, and several continental-European countries.  Expenses are recorded each calendar year and expressed in millions of U.S. dollars.

Tools
You do NOT have direct SQL access.  Instead, you can invoke the following helper functions; combine them as needed to derive new insights.

1. list_regions() -> List[str]
   Return every geographical region for which any data exist.
2. get_region_id(name: str) -> int
   Translate a human-readable region name into its internal identifier.
3. list_years() -> List[int]
   List all calendar years present in the database.
4. get_calendar_year_id(year: int) -> int
   Obtain the internal identifier for a specific calendar year.
5. list_plan_type_codes() -> List[str]
   Return the short codes of all plan types (e.g. "DC" for defined contribution).
6. get_plan_type_id(code: str) -> int
   Translate a plan-type code into its internal identifier.
7. get_expense(region_id: int, year_id: int, plan_type_id: int) -> float
   Fetch the expense (in millions of USD) for the given region/year/plan-type trio.
8. compute_average(values: List[float]) -> float
   Compute the arithmetic mean of a list of numeric values.

Additional (potentially useful but not always necessary) helpers
• get_total_expense_region_year(region_name: str, year: int) -> float
• convert_currency(amount: float, from_currency: str = "USD", to_currency: str = "EUR") -> float

Question
Considering the years 2016–2018, what is the average expense for the significant plans in the U.K.?

When you have collected all the information you need, output ONLY the final numeric answer (truncate, not round, to two decimal places) so that it can be automatically verified.
